s7.title: Insane Gripper and Positioning by 4678 CyberCavs

demand.text: In the Waterloo match that set a world record, a host says it concentrated on coral and filling the reef while its partner 3683 took the algae.

auto.text: In two Waterloo matches it and 3683 scored seven coral between them in auto.
A poster reports an eight-piece auto between the two in a Waterloo playoff match.

cycle.text: It drives up to the feeder station and shoves a coral down the chute straight into the end effector. The operator picks a branch and a level on a custom controller; a distance sensor and a camera align the robot to the reef.

endgame.text: A gas spring pushes the climber out, its jaws grab the cage and a motor winds it in; a ratchet holds once power is cut.
A host shows it on a deep climb in two Waterloo matches.

fallback.text: One controller button forces a position if auto align does not work.
With a coral on the floor between it and the station, pushing hard enough should still get the coral into the chute.

changed.text: Eight iterations of the end effector: the first was heavy, one had the coral pivot too far back, the fourth had four wheels that gripped only at their edges.
Bevel gears went from all ABS to UHMW hubs and nylon next to the motor.

outcome.text: 50-3-0 in official play; won the Ontario District Championship; did not play in a championship division.

functions.name: Chute

solves.text: Get coral from the feeder station into the end effector as fast as possible

functions.type: coral chute on gas shocks, released by the arm

facts.text: Starts within the bumpers, hooked on the arm, and comes out when the arm rises
Gas shocks let the robot ram the station: they absorb some of the blow and give more time

functions.name: Cantilevered arm
functions.type: elevator at one side with an arm on its end

facts.text: Rest to L4 in about

functions.name: End effector

solves.text: Hold coral well, weigh less than the first version and take coral anywhere along it

functions.type: three-wheel coral gripper driven by printed bevel gears

facts.text: Three wheels hold the coral; the current version holds it really well
Bevel gears: ABS with a milled UHMW hub, and nylon next to the motor
All-ABS hubs broke too quickly
PETG with carbon fiber was too brittle and sheared its teeth; nylon gives a little under torque
Not too hard to fix if a bevel gear breaks

cost.text: A little heavier than the four-wheel version, which held the coral poorly

solves.text: Clear algae from the reef, and score the processor when coopertition points are needed

facts.text: Swings the arm up to knock off high algae, and brings it down to take low algae off and throw it aside
Pulls algae from the floor onto the bumper, where two bars hold it

functions.name: Climber

solves.text: Grab the cage in a consistent place and stay up when power is cut

functions.type: gas-spring jaws with a winch and a power-off ratchet

facts.text: A gas spring pushes it out and elastics open the jaws
Feet rest on the bottom of the cage so the claws do not slide
Slanted polycarbonate sheets guide the cage between the jaws
A Kraken winds Dyneema cord on a spool
A solenoid pushes into the ratchet when power is cut

cost.text: Someone has to reset the ratchet after the match

solves.text: Align with the branch the operator picked

facts.text: A distance sensor, captioned "LAR", feeds a P loop towards the reef
A camera gives the yaw to the tag; trigonometry gives the sideways distance, corrected for rotation error, for a PD loop
Each reef button sets the tag, the side to approach and the rotation

solves.text: Pick a reef position and a level

facts.text: A ring of buttons stands for the reef, with four level buttons, rest and intake
Climber buttons sit behind a lock switch, and the climber locks when the robot is disabled

cost.text: Meant to be handheld, it was not as comfortable as expected and stays on the driver station

decisions.because: with four wheels the coral met only the edges of the wheels and was not held well

decisions.choice: Nylon bevel gears next to the motor
decisions.because: nylon moves a little under torque and does not shear
decisions.instead_of: PETG with carbon fiber, which is stronger but too brittle

decisions.choice: UHMW hubs in the bevel gears
decisions.because: printed ABS hubs broke too quickly
